title: Henriette de Clèves and Renato Birago to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, September 1574, BnF fr. 3315 ff. 15-16, 21

documents.shelfmark: BnF français 3315 ff. 15-16 (Gallica btv1b90600800 images f17-f18)

plaintext.source: contemporary or near-contemporary interlinear decipherment and original clear ending

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, 4000-pixel openings and enlarged overlapping crops
transcription.notes: Cipher is sharp, but the much smaller interlinear decipherment is overwritten, crowded and locally faded. Secure opening and clear ending recorded; no continuous diplomatic transcription claimed.

documents.shelfmark: BnF français 3315 f. 21 (Gallica btv1b90600800 images f23-f24)

plaintext.source: complete contemporary clear fair copy under the cipher flap

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, 4000-pixel opening and enhanced crop
transcription.notes: Complete transcription; one short expression in the first sentence remains uncertain.

system.summary: Graphic substitution alphabet with special doubled-letter signs and nulls; close to, but not identical with, Nevers collection no. 2 of 1584.

diacritics.note: Related key uses marked or compound signs for doubled consonants.

system.sibling_key: Nevers collection no. 2, BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 (1584); similar but not exact. Tomokiyo notes F=e and 9=q on the 1574 leaves, with x, y, z in clear.
system.notes: The exact 1574 table was not reconstructed. The target supplies stronger evidence than the sibling: an interlinear decipherment on f. 15 and a parallel clear copy on f. 21.

prior_solution.where: The manuscript itself preserves a contemporary interlinear decipherment on f. 15, a clear ending on f. 16r, and a complete clear copy under the cipher flap on f. 21; Tomokiyo described the system but published no reading.

conditions.human_role: The human selected the target and requested a solve/read followed by a write-up. No target-specific transcription or cryptanalytic intervention.

solution.what: Mapped manuscript folios to Gallica openings and fetched full-resolution images of ff. 15 and 21 and the neighbouring keys.
Found and transcribed the complete clear Italian fair copy beneath Birago's cipher flap at f. 21.
Identified the small writing between the cipher lines of f. 15 as a contemporary word-by-word decipherment, not random pen trials.
Fetched Nevers no. 2 of 1584 from BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 and confirmed that it is only a sibling key, not the exact target alphabet.
Checked a superficially similar Henri III appeal printed by Lavisse and rejected it as a crib because it predates this letter and has a different sender.
Read the opening on f. 15 and the clear ending on f. 16r; continuous transcription of the cipher leaves remained blocked by the overwritten minute hand.

outcome.fraction_read_source: f. 21 is complete (271 whitespace-delimited words in the transcribed quotation); the f. 15 opening and f. 16 clear ending are legible, but most of the two dense cipher pages are not continuously transcribed. The 0.4 is a rough page-and-text-weighted estimate, not a token count.
outcome.notes: The target is not wholly undecrypted: both leaves preserve their own reading aids. f. 21 is complete; f. 15 remains palaeographically incomplete.

gaps.detail: Minute interlinear French is crossed by larger cipher signs and locally faded; enlarged crop pass recovered anchors but not a defensible continuous text.
1584 Nevers no. 2 is similar but differs. Exact table could be rebuilt by glyph-level alignment of the f. 21 cipher slip with its interlinear Italian gloss.
Fair copy appears to read 'per saluato suo'; perhaps a personal name or abbreviation.
